contradiction_resolution: CONFIRMED by the author of the cited theorem himself, so the evidence class rises from adversarial_review to primary_source. (1) Core clause: Broaddus (arXiv:0711.0011v3 = Duke Math. J. 161 (2012) 1943-1969), Remark 4.4, verbatim: 'A natural first guess at a single generator for St(Sigma_g^1) is the arc system coming from the standard identification of the 4g-gon which corresponds to the labelled chord diagram in Figure 6, but in fact by Proposition 4.5 below, the class of this 0-filling system is trivial in St(Sigma_g^1)'; Figure 6 is captioned 'A trivial class in St(Sigma_g^1)'. The finding's terminology matches the source exactly: 'a filling arc system k-fills Sigma_g^1 if the arc system has 2g+k arcs', so a 0-filling system has exactly 2g arcs. (2) Second clause: Main Theorem 1.1, 'The homology class [phi_0] in St(Sigma_g^1) (resp. [phi_0] in St(Sigma_g)) is nontrivial for g >= 1', and Main Theorem 1.2, 'For g >= 1 the Steinberg module St(Sigma) is a cyclic Mod(Sigma)-module generated by the single element described in Section 4' (the Figure 5 diagram phi_0, distinct from Figure 6). This confirms the finding and strengthens it: because St is nonzero while the standard class is zero, the standard system provably cannot be a cyclic generator, so the defect is not merely that a symmetry argument is uninformative. (3) Independent coinvariant-level cross-check, not requiring the unretrieved Proposition 4.5: Church-Farb-Putman (arXiv:1108.0622v3 = IMRN 2012, no. 21, 5025-5030) Theorem 2(iii), attributed to Broaddus, states that a disconnected 0-filling system maps to 0 in U_0/partial(U_1) = (St_g)_{Mod_g}, where 'U is disconnected if the set t_1 u ... u t_n in D^2 is not connected'. The standard 4g-gon diagram has chords joining sides {1,3},{2,4},{5,7},{6,8},...; the two chords of a handle cross, but distinct handles do not interleave, so the union has g components and is disconnected for every g >= 2. Its image in the coinvariants therefore vanishes independently. (4) Mechanism correction the finding does not state: CFP do not derive vanishing from a mapping class acting by -1 on the generator. They compute partial(Y) = 2X + sum_{i=3}^{2g-1} (-1)^{i-1} partial_i Y with all partial_i Y disconnected, giving 2[X] = 0, and partial(Z) = (2g+1)X, giving (2g+1)[X] = 0, whence [X] = 0 by gcd(2,2g+1) = 1. Note [X] = 0 holds only in the coinvariants; [X] is nonzero in St by Main Theorem 1.1. An adjudicator must not conflate the finding's assertion (zero in St) with CFP's conclusion (zero in (St)_G); the finding's is strictly stronger and is the one the source states for the standard system. (5) Scope, and why the obstruction is broader than stated: even repaired to use phi_0, the published route does not reach (g,n) = (6,6). Broaddus cyclicity is stated only for Sigma_g and Sigma_g^1; CFP's vanishing covers Mod_g, Mod_{g,*} (vcd 4g-3) and Mod_{g,1} with one boundary component (cd 4g-2), always with trivial coefficients. CFP do record Harer duality with coefficients, 'for nu = vcd(Mod_{g,*}) = 4g-3 we have H^{nu-k}(Mod_{g,*};M tensor Q) = H_k(Mod_{g,*}; M tensor St_g tensor Q)', but their vanishing computation is for M = Q: the relations 2[X] = 0 and (2g+1)[X] = 0 come from boundaries of 1-filling systems and become twisted by the action on M, so nothing in the published argument computes (St tensor V)_G for nontrivial V. Cyclicity alone only reduces (St tensor V)_G to a quotient of V; the stabiliser and boundary relations must still be evaluated. (6) Corroboration: Irmer (arXiv:2312.08721v1) proves Broaddus's conjectural characterisation of the unique generating orbit and that Mod_g acts on St with trivial kernel, consistent with phi_0, not the standard system, being the generator. (7) No claim contradiction: no record in data/claims.jsonl (CONJ-0001, THM-0001..THM-0007, OBS-0001, RED-0001) concerns the Steinberg module or top-degree mapping class group cohomology, so contradicts_claim_ids remains empty. The finding is consistent with adjudicated FND-0035 (required ordinary degree equals vcd = 26 for (6,6); no arbitrary-puncture top-vcd vanishing theorem asserted) and with retired FND-0018. (8) No merge: the only other Steinberg-related record in proof/findings.jsonl is FND-0018, which is retired and asserts something different (applicability of CFP to punctured cases), so merge_target_id is null and the equivalence group standard-filling-system-null-in-Steinberg is unique. (9) Limits of this audit, stated so the gate is not misled: ATT-0043 and REV-0059 were not supplied, so the attribution that the attempt actually used the standard filling system as a cyclic generator fixed by handle half-turns could not be checked; only the finding's mathematical content was audited, and that content is correct. Proposition 4.5 of Broaddus could not be retrieved verbatim (ar5iv truncation), which is why the verified genus range is restricted to g >= 2 rather than the paper's standing g >= 1. Recommended promotion is therefore of the statement as scoped in the scope field: replace 'St of Mod_{g,1}/Mod_g' with 'St(Sigma_g^1) for g >= 2', which is exactly the primary-source assertion and covers the campaign case. (10) content_sha256 is null in every source record: this workspace exposes no shell or hashing tool, so no digest could be computed; recording a fabricated 64-hex string would falsify provenance and was refused. URLs, arXiv versions and DOIs are recorded instead and are sufficient to re-retrieve the quoted text.

scope.asserted_but_not_verified_verbatim: the closed-surface clause 'St of ... Mod_g': Remark 4.4 as retrieved names only St(Sigma_g^1); Proposition 4.5, which it cites, could not be retrieved verbatim (ar5iv rendering truncates before it), so the Sigma_g analogue and the g=1 boundary case are not confirmed here. At g=1 the standard 4-gon diagram is connected and would coincide with phi_0 up to labelling, so the zero-class claim should not be read as covering g=1.
scope.out_of_scope_for_the_campaign_target: Broaddus cyclicity (Main Theorem 1.2) covers only Sigma_g and Sigma_g^1; CFP's vanishing covers Mod_g (4g-5), Mod_{g,*} (vcd 4g-3, rational) and Mod_{g,1} with one boundary component (cd 4g-2, integral), all with trivial coefficients. Neither covers n >= 2 marked points nor computes (St tensor V)_G for a nontrivial coefficient system V, which is what the (6,6) corner requires.
scope.target_degree_context: vcd(M_{6,6}) = 4g-4+n = 26, the packet's ordinary_cohomology_degree; consistent with adjudicated FND-0035.
scope.verified_object: St(Sigma_g^1) = H~_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_g^1);Z), equivalently H~_{2g-2}(A_inf) = H_{2g-1}(A/A_inf) in the arc-complex model (Broaddus, Sections 2-3, eqs. (3) and (6))
scope.verified_statement: The 0-filling system of exactly 2g arcs given by the standard 4g-gon side identification (Broaddus Figure 6) is the zero class of St(Sigma_g^1); Broaddus's cyclic generator is the distinct chord diagram phi_0 (Figure 5), which is nonzero (Main Theorem 1.1). Hence the standard system generates only 0 and cannot be a cyclic generator, and any invariance/anti-invariance property of it (e.g. under handle half-turns) is vacuous.
